The core challenge lies in organizing chaotic sensory inputs into an ordered spatial framework. The primitive 'sensory_space_integration' formalizes this by treating each sensation as an extent S_i within a broader consciousness manifold C, which must be structured into a unified world W. This process mirrors Bayesian belief updating where prior sensory data is integrated with cognitive priors to yield a coherent spatial model. The 'spatial_interfusion' primitive captures how multiple sensory spaces interpenetrate rather than merely coexist, suggesting a non-Euclidean embedding where sensory extents are not independent but share a common objective world W. The 'perceptual_attention_bias' introduces a key constraint: attention acts as a selector that emphasizes certain sensory locations while suppressing others, leading to a biased perception of spatial relationships. These primitives form a triadic structure: sensory input → cognitive integration → selective attention. Failure modes arise when sensory extents cannot be meaningfully ordered (integration breakdown), when modalities fail to align (interfusion collapse), or when attention fails to focus appropriately (bias instability).
